tldr: Headlines across 11 country-buckets universally foreground Israel's retaliatory airstrikes on southern Lebanon and the deaths of two Israeli soldiers; Germany and Israeli outlets add a distinct legal framing foregrounding Hezbollah's ceasefire violation as justification, while wire services, Singapore/Vietnam, and India keep U.S.-mediated Rome talks in the headline as a contrasting backdrop to the violence.

evidence.quote: IDF begins targeted strikes in southern Lebanon
Two Israeli soldiers killed in Lebanon
2 Israeli soldiers killed in explosive device blast
Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers killed
Israeli army escalates strikes in south Lebanon
Israel carries out heaviest bombardment of Lebanon
in retaliation for Hezbollah ceasefire violations

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline in the corpus to frame the strikes using an intensity superlative — 'heaviest bombardment of Lebanon since June truce' — foregrounding scale and historical comparison rather than the soldier-death trigger or ceasefire-violation legal rationale used by all other outlets.

Only outlet to devote a standalone headline to civilian displacement — '360,000 Lebanese remain displaced' — absent from all international outlets including UK liberal broadsheets, making the humanitarian scope of the conflict invisible at the headline layer except within Israeli domestic coverage.

The only headline to adopt IDF-attributed language ('targeted strikes') without naming any trigger — no soldier deaths, no ceasefire violation, no diplomatic context — presenting the operation as an unprovoked opening action rather than a retaliation.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the dominant advertised story is Israeli retaliatory strikes following soldier deaths, with the Rome peace talks appearing as a pointed ironic counterpoint rather than a main narrative — a juxtaposition that recurs across wire services, Singapore, and India but is absent from the more militarily-focused UK, pan-Arab, and Russian headlines.
